title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned the Type Specimen. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Interface Specimen
options.lineage: Foundry type specimen books (Klim, Grilli Type, Dinamo): a face proven by showing it in use
options.thesis: Each product is a specimen spread: its own typeface, palette and live UI shown in use, like a foundry proves a font.
materials: each spread repaints to its product's own palette
one variable grotesque in every width
options.viewport: Your name set huge, one line on Cisco + 2026 products, CTAs; below, a specimen index where each product name is set in its own typeface with palette chips and a preview plate on hover.
options.risk: Three products have Spanish UIs; the repaint between spreads must keep AA contrast and not feel like five different sites.

options.label: Seven-Segment Readout
options.thesis: Your hard numbers (100k rows, 60 FPS, 262 tests) lit as segment readouts on a matte black instrument panel.
options.case: Fuses as a detail, not a world: great for metrics, but it can't show five product UIs and reads gimmicky to recruiters.

options.label: Endurance Livery Garage
options.lineage: Gulf / Martini racing liveries, number roundels, pit boards
options.thesis: Each project is a numbered car with its own livery stripe; the career is the race log.
options.case: Bold and memorable, but the racing costume competes with the product screenshots that should lead.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black-and-white barcode fields as the backdrop to a live 100k-row data demo.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pure monochrome can't show your products' own palettes, which are the main proof.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic senior-dev portfolio (hero, experience timeline, project cards) at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name + title + short intro, then experience list and a grid of project cards with screenshots.
canonCard.risk: Looks like many other candidates' sites; relies entirely on content to stand out.
